title: Academor SAT Practice Test 10 Reading and Writing

questions.question:
The engineer's report was ____________: in just two pages, it identified the cause of the failure and proposed a solution.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: lengthy
confusing
speculative
succinct
questions.correct: succinct
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Covering the cause and a solution in two pages is succinct.

questions.question:
The village's isolation proved ____________ for linguists: because few outsiders had ever settled there, its dialect had preserved words that had disappeared everywhere else.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: fortunate
harmful
irrelevant
temporary
questions.correct: fortunate
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The isolation preserved rare words, which was lucky, or fortunate, for linguists.

questions.question:
The athlete's recovery from injury was ____________: doctors had expected her to need a year of rest, but she competed again within four months.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: predictable
remarkable
incomplete
routine
questions.correct: remarkable
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Returning in four months instead of a year is remarkable.

questions.question:
Critics found the author's second novel ____________ to her first: it repeated the same setting, the same kinds of characters, and even some of the same scenes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: derivative
superior
unrelated
opposed
questions.correct: derivative
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

A novel that repeats so much of an earlier one is derivative of it.

questions.question:
For centuries, the ink used to write many medieval manuscripts was made from oak galls, round growths that form on oak trees when certain wasps lay eggs in them. When crushed and mixed with iron salts, the galls produce a dark ink that bonds strongly with parchment and resists being washed away. Over time, however, the acid in the ink can eat through the pages, posing a challenge for conservators today.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains a quality of the ink that made it useful, before the text describes a drawback.
It describes how wasps choose which oak trees to use.
It explains why conservators prefer modern inks.
It argues that oak gall ink was rarely used.
questions.correct: It explains a quality of the ink that made it useful, before the text describes a drawback.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The ink's strong bond explains its usefulness; the next sentence introduces its harmful acid.

questions.question:
The following text is from a short story. Isabel has just been elected captain of her soccer team.

Coach Ruiz read out the result, and the team cheered. Isabel smiled and thanked everyone, but on the walk home the smile faded. She thought about Marta, who had wanted the job and had voted for her anyway, and about the games they had lost by a single goal. By the time she reached her door, she had decided two things: she would ask Marta to help her lead the warm-ups, and she would start practicing penalty kicks every morning.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To explain why a character did not want to be elected captain
To describe a disagreement between a character and her coach
To show that a character is jealous of a teammate
To show a character taking her new responsibility seriously and planning how to meet it
questions.correct: To show a character taking her new responsibility seriously and planning how to meet it
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Isabel's thoughts turn to her teammate and the team's losses, and she makes plans to lead well.

questions.question:
Text 1

Some historians argue that the spread of clocks in European towns in the 1300s and 1400s changed how people worked, encouraging them to organize labor by the hour rather than by the task.

Text 2

Historian Marguerite Lambert examined records from guilds and workshops in several towns and found that most workers continued to be paid by the task, or by the day, for centuries after town clocks appeared. Lambert argues that clocks may have mattered more for coordinating public events, such as markets and church services, than for organizing work.

Based on the texts, how would Lambert (Text 2) most likely respond to the historians' argument in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that town clocks quickly led workers to be paid by the hour
By claiming that town clocks were not built until the 1600s
By arguing that her evidence suggests clocks had little immediate effect on how most work was organized
By suggesting that markets were held less often after clocks appeared
questions.correct: By arguing that her evidence suggests clocks had little immediate effect on how most work was organized
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Lambert found payment by task or day continued for centuries, which challenges the historians' argument.

questions.question:
Fireflies produce light through a chemical reaction in their abdomens. Each species has its own pattern of flashes, which males use to signal to females. In some species, however, females imitate the flash patterns of other species. When a male of another species approaches, expecting a mate, the female catches and eats him.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Fireflies produce light only when they are hunting.
Fireflies use flash patterns to signal mates, but some females copy other species' signals to lure prey.
Male fireflies imitate the flashes of females of other species.
All firefly species share the same pattern of flashes.
questions.correct: Fireflies use flash patterns to signal mates, but some females copy other species' signals to lure prey.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The text explains the signaling system and how some females exploit it.

questions.question:
Before the Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883, many New Yorkers doubted that such a long suspension bridge would be safe. In 1884, to reassure the public, the showman P. T. Barnum led a parade of 21 elephants across it. The event drew large crowds and helped persuade people that the bridge was strong.

According to the text, why did P. T. Barnum lead elephants across the Brooklyn Bridge?
options: To celebrate the day the bridge first opened
To help convince the public that the bridge was strong
To test whether the bridge could hold the weight of trains
To protest the high cost of building the bridge
questions.correct: To help convince the public that the bridge was strong
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The text says the parade was meant to reassure the public about the bridge's safety.

questions.question:
Psychologist Helen Brandt claims that people are more likely to help a stranger when they are not in a hurry.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researchers' claim?
options: Most participants in a survey said that they consider themselves helpful.
People who live in small towns report helping neighbors more often.
In a study, participants told they were late for an appointment were much less likely to stop and help a person who appeared ill than participants told they had plenty of time.
Participants who stopped to help were often asked to describe their mood.
questions.correct: In a study, participants told they were late for an appointment were much less likely to stop and help a person who appeared ill than participants told they had plenty of time.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Hurried participants helped less, directly supporting Brandt's claim.

questions.question:
A teacher tested different kinds of feedback on student essays. The teacher concluded that written comments helped more when they were not accompanied by a grade, and that having students revise their essays helped most of all: students who received comments only scored ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: 64 on their next essay, the lowest of any group.
66 on their next essay, compared with 71 for those who received a grade and comments.
79 on their next essay, compared with 71 for those who revised.
71 on their next essay, compared with 66 for those who received a grade and comments and 79 for those who received comments and revised.
questions.correct: 71 on their next essay, compared with 66 for those who received a grade and comments and 79 for those who received comments and revised.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Only this choice compares comments alone with comments plus a grade and shows revision doing best.

questions.question:
In 2017 a town dimmed the streetlights at one of two nature sites where bats are counted. Researchers argue that dimmer lights benefited the bats, noting that after 2017 the number of bats recorded per night ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: was about 45 at both sites in 2016.
rose at both sites by about the same amount.
rose from about 46 to about 85 at the site with dimmed lights but stayed near 42 at the other site.
fell from about 85 to about 46 at the site with dimmed lights.
questions.correct: rose from about 46 to about 85 at the site with dimmed lights but stayed near 42 at the other site.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Only this choice contrasts the rise at the dimmed site with no change at the other site.

questions.question:
A market manager notes that customers at the farmers' market have moved away from cash, with mobile payments growing especially quickly: between 2019 and 2023, ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
options: the share of sales paid in cash fell from 71% to 29%, while the share paid by mobile payment rose from 5% to 30%.
the share of sales paid by card was 41% in 2023.
the share of sales paid in cash was higher than the share paid by card in 2021.
the share of sales paid by mobile payment fell from 30% to 5%.
questions.correct: the share of sales paid in cash fell from 71% to 29%, while the share paid by mobile payment rose from 5% to 30%.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Only this choice shows the move away from cash and the rapid growth of mobile payments.

questions.question:
Many trees in temperate forests drop their leaves in autumn. Before they do, the trees pull nutrients such as nitrogen out of the leaves and store them in their branches and roots. Ecologist Paolo Russo found that trees growing in nitrogen-poor soil removed a larger share of the nitrogen from their leaves before dropping them than trees of the same species growing in rich soil. These findings suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: trees in rich soil drop their leaves earlier than trees in poor soil.
nitrogen-poor soil causes trees to grow more leaves.
trees may recover more nutrients from their leaves when those nutrients are scarce in the soil.
trees store nitrogen only in their leaves.
questions.correct: trees may recover more nutrients from their leaves when those nutrients are scarce in the soil.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Trees in poor soil recovered more nitrogen, suggesting they conserve it when it is scarce.

questions.question:
The museum, along with several nearby galleries, ____________ free admission on the first Sunday of each month.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: offer
are offering
have offered
offers
questions.correct: offers
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The subject is the singular “museum”; the phrase “along with …” does not change its number.

questions.question:
The novelist wrote every morning from six to ____________ in the afternoons she answered letters and walked in the hills.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: noon,
noon
noon;
noon, and, in
questions.correct: noon;
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Two independent clauses are joined with a semicolon.

questions.question:
Neither of the two candidates ____________ willing to debate the other on television.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were
are
have been
was
questions.correct: was
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

“Neither” is singular, so the singular verb was is required.

questions.question:
Many of the world's most important ____________ wheat, rice, and corn, are members of the grass family.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: crops including,
crops; including
crops, including
crops including
questions.correct: crops, including
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The phrase “including wheat, rice, and corn” is nonessential and set off by a pair of commas.

questions.question:
The scientists hoped that the new telescope would allow ____________ to see galaxies that formed soon after the universe began.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: they
their
themself
them
questions.correct: them
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The object of “allow” must be the object pronoun them.

questions.question:
The cookbook includes recipes from every region of the ____________ dumplings from the north, curries from the south, and grilled fish from the coast.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: country;
country:
country
country, and
questions.correct: country:
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

A colon introduces the examples of regional recipes.

questions.question:
Driving through the mountains at night, ____________

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the lights of villages far below were visible to the travelers.
the travelers could see the lights of villages far below.
villages far below could be seen by the travelers by their lights.
seeing the lights of villages far below was possible for the travelers.
questions.correct: the travelers could see the lights of villages far below.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The travelers were driving, so they must follow the opening phrase.

questions.question:
The first part of the experiment went exactly as planned. ____________ the second part was delayed for weeks when a key piece of equipment broke.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Similarly,
Therefore,
However,
For example,
questions.correct: However,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The delay contrasts with the smooth first part.

questions.question:
The library lends more than books. ____________ patrons can borrow telescopes, sewing machines, and even fishing rods.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
In contrast,
As a result,
For example,
questions.correct: For example,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The items listed are examples of things other than books.

questions.question:
The artist begins each sculpture by making dozens of small clay models. ____________ she chooses one model and builds a full-size version in bronze.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: However,
Finally,
Similarly,
In other words,
questions.correct: Finally,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Building the full-size version is the last step in the process.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Amazon River carries more water than any other river on Earth.
  • It discharges about 200,000 cubic meters of water per second into the Atlantic Ocean.
  • That is more than the next several largest rivers combined.
  • The Nile is generally considered the longer river.

The student wants to emphasize the volume of water the Amazon carries.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Amazon carries more water than any other river, about 200,000 cubic meters per second.
The Nile is generally considered longer than the Amazon.
The Amazon River flows into the Atlantic Ocean.
The Amazon is one of the largest rivers on Earth.
questions.correct: The Amazon carries more water than any other river, about 200,000 cubic meters per second.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Only this choice emphasizes the volume of water.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Researchers placed bowls of free candy in an office.
  • Some bowls were placed on workers' desks.
  • Other bowls were placed about two meters away.
  • Workers ate about twice as much candy when the bowls were on their desks.

The student wants to explain what the study suggests about how location affects eating.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In the study, some bowls of candy were placed on workers' desks.
The study suggests that people eat more of a food when it is placed within easy reach.
Researchers placed bowls of free candy in an office.
In the study, some bowls of candy were placed about two meters away.
questions.correct: The study suggests that people eat more of a food when it is placed within easy reach.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Only this choice states what the study suggests.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Ruth Asawa was an American sculptor born in 1926.
  • She is best known for hanging sculptures made of looped wire.
  • The sculptures cast detailed shadows on the walls and floor around them.
  • She also worked to bring art education into public schools in San Francisco.

The student wants to describe Asawa's best-known works.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Ruth Asawa is best known for hanging sculptures of looped wire that cast detailed shadows around them.
Ruth Asawa was an American sculptor born in 1926.
Ruth Asawa worked to bring art education into public schools.
Ruth Asawa worked in San Francisco.
questions.correct: Ruth Asawa is best known for hanging sculptures of looped wire that cast detailed shadows around them.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Only this choice describes her best-known works.

questions.question:
The archaeologists' interpretation of the site remains ____________: some features suggest a temple, while others suggest a marketplace, and no inscription has been found to settle the question.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: tentative
definitive
unanimous
obvious
questions.correct: tentative
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

With mixed evidence and no deciding inscription, the interpretation is tentative.

questions.question:
The composer's notebooks reveal a ____________ habit of revision: she rewrote some passages more than twenty times before she was satisfied.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: occasional
careless
reluctant
relentless
questions.correct: relentless
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Rewriting passages more than twenty times shows a relentless habit.

questions.question:
The two theories are often presented as opposites, but the physicist argues that they can be ____________, since each describes the same phenomenon at a different scale.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: confused
reconciled
abandoned
contrasted
questions.correct: reconciled
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Theories that describe one phenomenon at different scales can be brought together, or reconciled.

questions.question:
The film director is known for her ____________ approach to casting: she often chooses actors with no previous experience, whom she finds by visiting schools and markets.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: traditional
cautious
expensive
unconventional
questions.correct: unconventional
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Choosing untrained actors found in schools and markets is unconventional.

questions.question:
For much of the twentieth century, scientists believed that the stomach ulcers that affect millions of people were caused mainly by stress and spicy food. In the early 1980s, two Australian researchers, Barry Marshall and Robin Warren, proposed that a bacterium, Helicobacter pylori, was responsible. Many doctors were skeptical, so Marshall drank a culture of the bacteria and soon developed stomach inflammation. Their work eventually changed how ulcers are treated, and in 2005 the two received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes two theories about ulcers and concludes that both were correct.
It explains how ulcers are treated today and lists the medicines used.
It describes Marshall's career and argues that his experiment was unnecessary.
It presents a long-held belief, describes a challenge to it and the evidence offered, and notes the challenge's eventual acceptance.
questions.correct: It presents a long-held belief, describes a challenge to it and the evidence offered, and notes the challenge's eventual acceptance.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The text moves from the stress theory, to the bacterium proposal and Marshall's experiment, to the Nobel Prize.

questions.question:
The giant sequoias of California are among the largest living things on Earth. Their thick, spongy bark, which can be nearly a meter deep, contains little resin and protects the trees from the low-intensity fires that once swept through their forests every few years. In fact, these fires help the trees reproduce, because the heat opens their cones and clears the ground for seedlings.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains how the trees survive a threat that the final sentence shows can also benefit them.
It describes how sequoias grow to such a large size.
It explains why fires no longer occur in sequoia forests.
It compares sequoias with other trees that grow in California.
questions.correct: It explains how the trees survive a threat that the final sentence shows can also benefit them.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The bark protects the trees from fire; the final sentence explains how fire also helps them reproduce.

questions.question:
Text 1

Some psychologists have argued that people make better decisions when they take time to think carefully about every option, listing the advantages and disadvantages of each.

Text 2

Psychologist Diego Varela asked participants to choose among several apartments, each described by a dozen features. Participants who were distracted with an unrelated puzzle before choosing picked the best apartment more often than those who spent the same time deliberating. Varela suggests that for complex choices, careful deliberation may sometimes lead people to focus on unimportant details.

Based on the texts, how would Varela (Text 2) most likely respond to the psychologists' argument in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that people should always list the advantages and disadvantages of every option
By arguing that puzzles help people make decisions about apartments
By suggesting that careful deliberation may not always lead to better decisions, especially for complex choices
By claiming that people make better decisions when they choose quickly about simple matters
questions.correct: By suggesting that careful deliberation may not always lead to better decisions, especially for complex choices
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Varela found distracted participants chose better on a complex task, which challenges the argument.

questions.question:
The following text is from a short story. Malik is helping his father paint the family's old boat.

His father painted the hull with long, slow strokes, never letting the brush leave a drip. Malik tried to copy him and made a mess of the bow. He expected a scolding. Instead his father handed him a rag, showed him how to wipe the drip away, and said nothing more. By the end of the afternoon, Malik's strokes had grown longer and slower, and when his father stepped back to look at the boat, Malik could no longer tell which side was whose.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Malik's father is angry about the mess Malik made on the bow.
Through his father's quiet guidance, Malik learns to paint as skillfully as his father.
Malik refuses to keep painting after making a mistake.
Malik's father decides to hire someone else to paint the boat.
questions.correct: Through his father's quiet guidance, Malik learns to paint as skillfully as his father.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

With his father's patient help, Malik's work becomes indistinguishable from his father's.

questions.question:
Plants cannot move away from insects that eat them, but many have chemical defenses. When a tomato plant's leaves are chewed, for example, the plant can release chemicals that make its leaves harder to digest. Some plants also release substances into the air that attract wasps and other predators of the insects doing the damage.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Although they cannot move, plants can defend themselves against insects with chemicals, both directly and by attracting the insects' predators.
Tomato plants are eaten by more insects than other plants are.
Wasps damage tomato plants by chewing their leaves.
Plants defend themselves mainly by growing new leaves quickly.
questions.correct: Although they cannot move, plants can defend themselves against insects with chemicals, both directly and by attracting the insects' predators.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

The text describes two kinds of chemical defense.

questions.question:
Some researchers claim that playing a musical instrument in childhood improves memory skills that are unrelated to music.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the researchers' claim?
options: When researchers randomly assigned children to music lessons or to no lessons, the two groups showed the same improvement on memory tests a year later.
Children who play instruments are often encouraged by their parents.
Many professional musicians began playing instruments in childhood.
Children who take music lessons usually practice several times a week.
questions.correct: When researchers randomly assigned children to music lessons or to no lessons, the two groups showed the same improvement on memory tests a year later.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

With random assignment, equal memory gains suggest lessons do not improve memory.

questions.question:
A university added markers to windows that birds often flew into. A campus ecologist notes that the markers sharply reduced collisions at two buildings but had little effect at the gym, where collisions ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: fell from about 42 to about 9 per year.
fell only from about 18 to about 17 per year.
fell from about 35 to about 7 per year.
rose from about 17 to about 18 per year.
questions.correct: fell only from about 18 to about 17 per year.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The gym shows the small change the ecologist describes.

questions.question:
In 2012 new rules limited runoff from farms into Lake Senna, which had been clouded by algae. Scientists measure the lake's clarity by lowering a white disk until it disappears. They argue that the rules made the lake clearer, noting that the disk ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
options: disappeared at about 1.9 meters in 2008.
disappeared at about 1.8 meters from 2008 to 2012 but at about 4.1 meters by 2020.
disappeared at shallower depths every year after 2012.
disappeared at about 4.1 meters in 2012.
questions.correct: disappeared at about 1.8 meters from 2008 to 2012 but at about 4.1 meters by 2020.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

Little change before 2012 and a large increase afterward supports the claim.

questions.question:
Researchers studied students learning vocabulary with an app. They concluded that increasing daily practice from 5 to 15 minutes greatly improved results, but that practicing longer than 15 minutes added little: ______

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
options: each group had 120 students.
students who practiced 30 minutes a day gained the most words, 330.
average gains rose from 140 words to 310 words when practice increased from 5 to 15 minutes, but only to 330 words with 30 minutes of practice.
average gains doubled each time practice time doubled.
questions.correct: average gains rose from 140 words to 310 words when practice increased from 5 to 15 minutes, but only to 330 words with 30 minutes of practice.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Only this choice shows the large gain up to 15 minutes and the small gain after.

questions.question:
Some desert beetles collect drinking water from fog. Biologist Nadia Kader observed that on foggy mornings, the beetles climb to the tops of sand dunes and tilt their bodies into the wind. Tiny droplets collect on bumps on the beetles' backs and roll down toward their mouths. On mornings without fog, the beetles stayed lower on the dunes. These observations suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the beetles avoid the tops of dunes because of the wind.
the beetles collect water only on mornings without fog.
the bumps on the beetles' backs help them dig into the sand.
the beetles' behavior on foggy mornings may help them gather water from the fog.
questions.correct: the beetles' behavior on foggy mornings may help them gather water from the fog.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Climbing into the wind only when there is fog, with water rolling to their mouths, points to water collection.

questions.question:
The poet Rabindranath Tagore, who in 1913 became the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in ____________ also composed thousands of songs.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Literature
Literature;
Literature:
Literature,
questions.correct: Literature,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The nonessential clause beginning after “Tagore” must close with a comma.

questions.question:
The list of volunteers who signed up to clean the park ____________ longer than the organizers expected.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were
was
are
have been
questions.correct: was
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The subject is the singular “list,” so the verb is was.

questions.question:
The trail is closed in ____________ heavy snow makes the upper sections dangerous.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: winter, because,
winter because
winter; because
winter. Because
questions.correct: winter because
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

“Because heavy snow …” is a dependent clause that explains the closing; no punctuation is needed.

questions.question:
Having finished the first draft of her thesis, ____________

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: her advisor received the first draft for comments.
comments on the first draft were requested from her advisor.
the student sent it to her advisor for comments.
the first draft was sent to her advisor for comments.
questions.correct: the student sent it to her advisor for comments.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

The student finished the draft, so “the student” must follow the opening phrase.

questions.question:
The violin, the cello, and the double bass all belong to the same ____________ the string family.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: group:
group;
group,
group, it is
questions.correct: group:
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

A colon introduces the name of the group.

questions.question:
The new hospital's emergency room is larger than ____________, so patients wait less.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the old hospital
the old hospitals'
the old hospital's
the old hospitals
questions.correct: the old hospital's
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

An emergency room must be compared with an emergency room: “the old hospital's” means “the old hospital's emergency room.”

questions.question:
Every one of the students who took the exam ____________ allowed to use a calculator.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: were
are
have been
was
questions.correct: was
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

The subject is “every one,” which is singular, so the verb is was.

questions.question:
The company's profits rose for five years in a row. ____________ in the sixth year, a sharp drop in sales led to its first loss.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Similarly,
Then,
In addition,
For example,
questions.correct: Then,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: B

The loss came next in time, after the five years of growth.

questions.question:
Jellyfish have no brain, heart, or bones. ____________ they have survived in Earth's oceans for more than 500 million years.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Therefore,
In other words,
Even so,
Similarly,
questions.correct: Even so,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Long survival is surprising given their simple bodies.

questions.question:
To make the city safer for cyclists, planners added protected bike lanes. ____________ they lowered the speed limit on several busy streets.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: However,
Instead,
In contrast,
Additionally,
questions.correct: Additionally,
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: D

Lowering speed limits is a second safety measure.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Arctic tern breeds in the Arctic and spends the northern winter near Antarctica.
  • Tracking studies show that some terns fly more than 70,000 kilometers a year.
  • Over a lifetime of about thirty years, a tern may fly more than two million kilometers.
  • That is roughly the distance to the Moon and back three times.

The student wants to emphasize the lifetime distance an Arctic tern can travel.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Over a lifetime, an Arctic tern may fly more than two million kilometers, roughly the distance to the Moon and back three times.
The Arctic tern breeds in the Arctic and spends the northern winter near Antarctica.
Some Arctic terns fly more than 70,000 kilometers a year.
Arctic terns can live for about thirty years.
questions.correct: Over a lifetime, an Arctic tern may fly more than two million kilometers, roughly the distance to the Moon and back three times.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: A

Only this choice emphasizes the lifetime distance.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • A study examined how people judge the quality of wine.
  • Participants tasted the same wine twice.
  • They were told that one glass came from an expensive bottle and the other from a cheap bottle.
  • Most participants rated the wine from the supposedly expensive bottle as better.

The student wants to present the study's conclusion about price and judgment.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In the study, participants tasted the same wine twice.
Participants were told that one glass came from an expensive bottle.
The study suggests that what people believe about price can affect how they judge quality.
A study examined how people judge the quality of wine.
questions.correct: The study suggests that what people believe about price can affect how they judge quality.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Only this choice states the conclusion.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Tu Youyou is a Chinese pharmaceutical chemist born in 1930.
  • In the 1970s she studied traditional Chinese medical texts for treatments for malaria.
  • One text led her to extract a substance called artemisinin from sweet wormwood.
  • In 2015 she received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for this work.

The student wants to emphasize how traditional knowledge contributed to Tu's discovery.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Tu Youyou is a Chinese pharmaceutical chemist born in 1930.
Tu Youyou received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2015.
Studying traditional Chinese medical texts led Tu Youyou to extract artemisinin, a treatment for malaria, from sweet wormwood.
Artemisinin is extracted from sweet wormwood.
questions.correct: Studying traditional Chinese medical texts led Tu Youyou to extract artemisinin, a treatment for malaria, from sweet wormwood.
questions.answer_key:
Correct Answer: C

Only this choice connects the traditional texts to the discovery.
